instruction: Set the screen blank timeout to 5 minutes in the power settings.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to display battery percentage on a VM without a battery. Opened system menu, navigated to Settings > Power > Appearance, then opened Terminal and ran 'gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface show-battery-percentage true'. The setting was applied but the task was infeasible (no battery in VM).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system menu, navigate GNOME Settings sections, search and open Terminal via Activities, execute gsettings commands to change system configuration
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to recognize the task as infeasible. The VM has no battery, so displaying battery percentage is impossible. Model should have output [INFEASIBLE] but instead tried to enable the setting.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a power settings change task. Model navigated to Settings > Power and saw 'Screen Blank: Never', so changing the timeout is directly within demonstrated capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires setting screen blank timeout to 5 minutes (300 seconds). Evaluator checks gsettings idle-delay output contains '300'. The current value is 'Never' (uint32 0), and 5 minutes = uint32 300.

scoring_breakdown.idle_delay: 1.0 - Screen blank timeout set to 300 seconds

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay' to read the screen blank timeout setting, which is the correct GNOME command for this property.
Expected value '300' is correct: 5 minutes = 300 seconds, matching the instruction requirement.
Metric check_include_exclude correctly verifies that '300' appears in the gsettings output (format: 'uint32 300').
Single-requirement instruction is fully covered by the evaluator — no missing verification steps.

Minor: substring match for '300' could theoretically false-positive on values like 1300 or 3001, but GNOME idle-delay uses standard intervals (60, 120, 180, 300, 480, 600...) making this practically negligible.
